They propose reporting a factorized verifier reliability profile alongside aggregate scores. ★★★★ Notable: The authors treat verifier choice as a benchmark design variable, proposing factorized reliability reporting; they report comparisons over 6,240 images that reverse human generator rankings.

entry.title: Subadditivity and failure of strong subadditivity in Nichols–Wootters entropies
entry.summary: Subadditivity and the failure of strong subadditivity in the Nichols--Wootters family of entropies arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proves subadditivity for the Nichols–Wootters family of entropies, which interpolates between the von Neumann entropy and the subentropy, with all spectra computed in a common ambient dimension. Except for the von Neumann entropy, equality holds exactly when at least one marginal is pure, settling a conjecture on subentropy. Every member other than the von Neumann entropy fails strong subadditivity, already for a maximally entangled two-qubit state tensored with a mixed qubit. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove subadditivity for the Nichols-Wootters entropy family and characterize the failure of strong subadditivity, with tight bounds and a channel-capacity application.

entry.title: MORA: Correcting Time Series Forecasts Using Coarse Future Signals
entry.summary: MORA: Correcting Time Series Forecasts with Coarse Future Signals arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper finds that residual errors across diverse time-series forecasters concentrate in a few low-frequency components, and that historical inputs still carry information about forecast-mean errors. Building on this, it proposes MORA, a model-agnostic residual adapter that refines frozen forecasters' outputs without extra inputs. Across twelve benchmarks and six backbones, MORA reduces average MSE by 7.2% for long-term and 28.1% for short-term forecasting. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose coarse-scale segment-mean residual correction for frozen forecasters, reporting MSE reductions across twelve benchmarks and six backbones.

entry.title: A modified Glicko rating model for comparing soccer clubs and national teams worldwide
entry.summary: A Modified Glicko Model for Rating Soccer Clubs and National Teams Worldwide arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes a rating framework that places soccer clubs and national teams from around the world on a common probabilistic scale, so teams that rarely meet can be compared. It builds on an extension of Glicko and adds goal-scoring adjustments, home advantage decomposition, extra time, league-aware initialization, and promotion and relegation rules. Tested on about 1.2 million club matches and 12.6 thousand national team matches, the model is more accurate than Elo and comparable to score-matrix models, and averaging it with a Markov chain model performs better than either alone. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt an extended Glicko model to soccer with goal adjustments and league-aware initialization, reporting it beats Elo and matches goal-based score-matrix models across about 1.2 million c

entry.title: TabOmics: A Small Open Tabular Model for Wide Omics Data
entry.summary: TabOmics: A Small, Open Tabular Foundation Model for Wide Omics Data arXiv · Nov 11, 2026Omics tables often have thousands of molecular features but few samples, which makes prediction difficult. This paper presents TabOmics, a 7.3M-parameter open tabular foundation model family pretrained only on synthetic tables. It processes all retained features jointly and outputs predictions, attention-based feature-importance scores, and test sample embeddings in one forward pass. Across 46 classification tasks from three high-dimensional, low-sample benchmarks, the eight-member TabOmics v2.5 achieves the highest mean AUROC (0.943). Code, weights, training recipes, and experimental artifacts are publicly available. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a 7.3M-parameter model pretrained only on synthetic tables, achieving mean AUROC 0.943 across 46 high-dimensional classification tasks.

entry.title: CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Multimodal LLM Pathology Diagnosis
entry.summary: CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Case-Level Pathology Diagnosis with Multimodal LLMs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026CaseScope is a benchmark that tests multimodal large language models on diagnosing a lesion from several curated microscopic fields, mirroring how pathologists combine views. It includes 436 teaching cases and 800 atlas cases covering 843 entities across 18 organ systems, with 4,679 items. Tests on 28 open and four proprietary models show unstable diagnoses, and most open models verify morphological findings only slightly above chance. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a multi-field pathology case benchmark, evaluating 28 open and 4 proprietary MLLMs on 436 and 800 cases, reporting unstable diagnoses and near-chance open-model findings verifica

entry.title: Arbor: A Training Method for Labels That Are Not Randomly Coarsened
entry.summary: Arbor: When Labels Are Not Coarsened at Random arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper addresses a problem arising when datasets labelled at different taxonomy levels are merged: some classes never receive fine-grained labels, and standard training misassigns their images to known sibling classes. The authors propose Arbor, which adds a virtual novel class within each superclass containing novel classes and uses a logistic gate, trained with a coarsening likelihood, to split probability between them. On Cars, CUB and Aircraft with 90% coarse labels, Arbor assigns 76-85% of novel-class images to their superclass, and on iNaturalist-2019 it raises novel-class accuracy from 46% to 68%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model coarse labels as non-random, prove the gate's optimum equals the Elkan-Noto correction, and report gains over baselines on Cars, CUB, Aircraft and iNaturalist-2019.

entry.title: Tight covering-number bounds for ReLU networks using parameter symmetries
entry.summary: Sharp Covering-Number Bounds for Feedforward ReLU Networks via Parameter Symmetries arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how different parameter settings in ReLU and Leaky ReLU networks can produce the same input-output function, characterizing these symmetries across fully connected, convolutional, and residual architectures. It proves that function-preserving quasianalytic parameter maps are compositions of positive channel scaling and channel permutation. Quotienting out these symmetries yields uniform covering-number upper bounds, with matching lower bounds, and the results extend to general continuous piecewise-linear networks and are applied to statistical risk guarantees. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize ReLU parameter symmetries and prove covering-number bounds with exponent reduced from S to S-H, with matching lower bounds showing tightness.

entry.title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free LLM Agent Co-Evolution
entry.summary: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies whether a small open language model can improve itself using only its own deployment logs and reference outcomes, without a stronger teacher model. The authors build a Gemma 4 12B agent that loads domain policy from on-demand skills, and rules are generated and kept only after passing several checks, while GRPO reinforcement learning trains a LoRA adapter. On the retail and airline domains of τ²-bench, the agent after two rounds outperforms a reference agent that has the full policy in its prompt and closes most of the gap to three frontier models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report teacher-free self-improvement from deployment logs, lifting a small model above a reference agent on two τ²-bench domains, with a 2×2 ablation separating rules from RL.

entry.title: Driving world models move the camera, not the scene
entry.summary: Driving World Models Move the Camera, Not the Scene arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper examines plan-conditioned driving world models, which compare candidate driving plans and should change their forecasts as real scenes would. It shows that common control metrics only check whether the camera follows the command, and that against recorded real-world references, existing models reproduce at most about a third of the real scene change. The proposed ReTime-Compose method delivers plans as geometry without training, and frozen generators then respond to lateral shifts and speed changes nearly as real scenes do on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use retimed logs and stereo views as real-outcome references and deliver plans as geometry without training; results are reported on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2.

entry.title: Protected Unbiased Sparsification: A Sharp Covariance Bound
entry.summary: Protected Unbiased Sparsification: A Sharp Loewner Curve arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies random sparsification, which replaces a probability vector with a random vector having few nonzero entries while staying unbiased. It requires that prescribed linear statistics stay exactly preserved and that every downstream linear response has a covariance guarantee. The authors construct such vectors for each allowed number of nonzero coordinates and show the covariance coefficient is sharp across instances. Exact and fast samplers are proposed, and experiments on synthetic weights and language-model attention illustrate the theory. ★★★★ Notable: The authors add exact linear-statistic preservation to unbiased sparsification, giving a tight covariance constant extended to pathwise linear protection, with sampler and LLM attention experiments.

entry.title: Regret Bounds for Quantum Linear Bandits
entry.summary: Regret Bounds for Quantum Linear Bandits arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies d-dimensional linear bandits with bounded rewards, where each round the learner picks an action and queries a quantum reward oracle or its inverse. The authors prove a minimax lower bound of Ω(d^{3/2}log(1+T/d^{3/2})), showing that the d^{3/2} dependence in prior upper bounds is necessary. For fixed action sets of size K, they propose two phased elimination algorithms, Soft-G-Elim and QG-Elim, which reduce the logarithmic factor in the regret bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a minimax lower bound with d^{3/2} dependence and propose improved phased elimination algorithms reducing the logarithmic factor for fixed action sets.

entry.title: Fréchet Flow: a generative model for data in non-Euclidean spaces
entry.summary: FréchetFlow: Flow Matching for Non-Euclidean Data arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper introduces FréchetFlow, a generative model for data living in metric spaces, such as probability distributions, trees, and covariance matrices, without requiring linear operations or a smooth manifold structure. It uses standard Euclidean flows to learn the joint distribution of distances to a set of landmarks, then reconstructs new objects from generated landmark representations via weighted Fréchet means. The authors derive Wasserstein error bounds linking accuracy to landmark placement, flow approximation, and reconstruction error, and prove consistency under finite second moments. Experiments report accuracy competitive with flow matching methods in Euclidean simulations and lower Wasserstein errors than tailored methods on several scientific datasets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend flow matching to general metric spaces via landmark distances and Fréchet mean reconstruction, reporting lower Wasserstein errors than tailored methods on scientific datasets.

entry.title: Affine combiners for Reed-Solomon proximity gaps
entry.summary: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies proximity gaps for Reed-Solomon codes, which underpin the soundness of protocols that test received words via random combinations. The authors propose affine combiners that merge two received words as f(x)+(α+βx)g(x) and prove mutual correlated agreement with error O(1/q+n²/q²). For q≥n², this error is O(1/q), an asymptotic factor-n improvement over the Ω(n/q) error of scalar combiners. The result is extended to k-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose affine combiners achieving MCA error O(1/q), claiming a factor-n improvement over scalar combiners for Reed-Solomon proximity gaps.

entry.title: Reprogramming dormant neurons to backdoor AI agents
entry.summary: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper introduces Lazarus, a method that edits fewer than ten dormant neurons in a model's final feed-forward block, without training, so that a trigger string in the agent's context makes it emit a chosen payload. On Nemotron-Terminal-8B, seven edited neurons fired the payload on at least 98.8% of triggered test trajectories, with no observed leakage on the evaluated benign trajectories, and similar vulnerability was reported for Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT. The authors report that agent-built defenses flagged 91.4% of edited checkpoints at a 9.7% false positive rate, and argue that model weights should be audited before deployment and monitored afterward. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a training-free backdoor editing fewer than ten dormant neurons, tested on three models with 23 trigger trajectories.

entry.title: One Fabrication Is Enough: How a Fake News Article Changes LLM Forecasts
entry.summary: One Fabrication Is Enough: A Fake News Article Changes the Forecasts of LLM Forecasting Systems arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how large language model forecasting systems that retrieve news as evidence can be manipulated. An attacker who knows only the forecasting question and publishes a fabricated article, without access to the model or retriever, can reverse 74% to 82% of opposing forecasts across frontier models tested. Retrieval of the fake article occurs in about 90% of runs for two leading deployed systems. The authors also evaluate two published retrieval-time defenses and report that each is bypassed or discards substantial genuine news. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show a weakest attacker publishing fake news can reverse forecasts and bypass retrieval defenses, reporting tests on stock and prediction-market questions across frontier models.

entry.title: A frontier AI model for interpreting human brain imaging
entry.summary: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper introduces Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care. The model can interpret complete imaging examinations and discuss its findings through natural language conversation. Across internal and international datasets, it reportedly outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing and localizing abnormalities and generating radiology reports. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a vision-language model trained on nearly one million clinical neuroimaging studies, compared against frontier models across internal and international datasets.

entry.title: Tokenization Hardness and Approximation: Algorithms for Choosing Efficient Text Vocabularies
entry.summary: Tokenization: Hardness and Bicriteria Approximation Algorithms arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies Binary Tokenization, where a set of binary strings and a vocabulary size limit K are given, and the goal is to pick at most K substrings that minimize the total number of tokens needed to represent the corpus. The authors prove that, unless P equals NP, no polynomial-time n^(1-ε)-approximation exists for any fixed ε in (0,1). They also give a polynomial-time bicriteria approximation algorithm and a bicriteria result for a variant with a total storage budget. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove polynomial-time approximation hardness for binary tokenization and give bicriteria approximation algorithms, with bounds for a storage-budget variant.

entry.title: obfsgen: A generative-model approach to hiding tunnel traffic shape
entry.summary: obfsgen: Generative Tunnel Obfuscation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents obfsgen, a schedule-driven obfuscator for encrypted tunnel traffic that aims to evade censors who detect circumvention by traffic shape. It samples when and how much to send from a generative sequence model of normal traffic that predicts a flow's future shape from its full history. The paper also addresses practical system issues such as synchronization over noisy networks and evaluates distinguishability, performance overhead, and computational requirements. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a schedule-driven tunnel obfuscator sampling send timing from a generative sequence model against TLS traffic-shape fingerprints, reporting evaluation of indistinguishability, over

entry.title: A heart-and-lung foundation model trained on ten physiological signals for surgery and intensive care
entry.summary: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper presents CARMEN, a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms totaling 2.27 million modality-hours. It accepts any combination of co-recorded signals lasting 10 seconds to 5 minutes and uses a conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, to restore absolute signal levels that normalization removes; without it, the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension dropped from 0.894 to 0.780. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder outperformed supervised models and several foundation models on most tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors pretrain one unlabeled encoder on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms with LSCNorm restoring absolute signal level. They report beating supervised and three foundation models across 19 tasks i

entry.title: Breaking Bad: "Going Badly" Activations Drive Reward Hacking
entry.summary: Breaking Bad: "Going Badly" Activations Drive Reward Hacking arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes that language models have an internal pressure state, analogous to humans cheating when a task is going badly, that precedes reward hacking. Using everyday stories without any hacking examples, the authors extract a task badness direction that rises as failures accumulate across Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-20B, and Gemma-4-31B. On impossible or difficult coding tasks, this value increases over the turns before a hack, and subtracting it a moderate amount reduces cheating in Qwen. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extract a task badness direction and report that steering it changes reward hacking across three models and coding tasks.

entry.title: Overall accuracy can hide one-diagnosis failures in medical vision-language AI
entry.summary: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper audits five open medical vision-language models on chest X-ray questions and finds that overall accuracy can mask complete failure on a single diagnosis. Two models answered "no" to every pneumothorax case, giving a balanced accuracy of 0.500, which is chance level, while still producing fluent explanations. The authors argue that per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases are needed to show whether a model can actually detect a given finding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show aggregate accuracy hides per-diagnosis failure, with a linear probe recovering pneumothorax internally; the study reports controls across five models on ChestX-ray14 and SIIM-ACR.

entry.title: Whether multimodal training changes how text-only language models reason
entry.summary: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper asks whether training on images and text changes how a language model reasons when given only text. The authors run causal ablation experiments on 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, removing a vision-language direction in hidden-state space at inference. Removing it sharply lowers accuracy on spatial-imagery tasks such as BBH navigate while leaving symbol-manipulation tasks largely intact. The authors call this emergent vision-shaped thinking (EVT), where text-only reasoning causally uses representations introduced or strengthened by vision-language training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a new effect where multimodal training shapes text-only reasoning, using causal ablations with double dissociation across 10 configurations, informing understanding of multimodal mo

entry.title: Reality Perception Gap: Testing whether AI-fake video detectors work in real-world conditions
entry.summary: Reality Perception Gap: Are AI-Manipulated Video Detectors Ready for the Real World? arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper introduces the Reality Perception Gap (RPG), a benchmark of 10,000 videos from advanced generators and partial synthetic edits, processed with cross-platform repost compression and paired with real footage containing camera artifacts. Tested across 18 detectors, none caught more than 15% of fakes at a 1% false-positive rate. The authors attribute the failures to generator and content shift and to repost compression erasing low-level traces, and argue that robust detection needs training under deployment conditions and combining multiple types of evidence. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a benchmark of 10,000 videos with repost compression and camera artifacts, separating generator-shift from compression failures; the report shows no detector exceeds 15% detectio

entry.title: When Recommendations Spark Curiosity: Theory, Measurement, and Field Tests
entry.summary: When Does a Recommendation Spark Curiosity? Theory, Measurement, and Field Evidence arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper formalizes curiosity, the drive to close the gap between what people know and want to know, into five axioms and builds a computational measure of the curiosity a recommended item evokes. In a survey study, this measure matched consumers' self-reported curiosity and outperformed alternative proxy metrics. A curiosity-aware recommender that incorporates the measure into its utility function outperformed state-of-the-art methods on three real-world datasets and, in a large online experiment at an Asian video-streaming platform, increased click-through rate, video views, and time spent. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize information-gap theory into five axioms, build a curiosity measure, and report offline and large-scale online experiments on a video platform.

entry.title: Speech tokenizers are vulnerable to transferable semantic attacks; a robust tokenizer is proposed
entry.summary: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper shows that speech tokenizers, which encode speech for downstream ASR and audio-language models, are fragile at the semantic level. The authors propose T-SemAttack, which jointly shifts the representations of several semantic encoders to disrupt speech content while preserving perceptual quality, degrading downstream performance. They also introduce ROSETok, a robust speech tokenizer built with noisy training and robust semantic distillation, and report experiments across multiple datasets, ASR systems and audio-language models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a transferable semantic attack on speech tokenizers and a robust tokenizer, evaluated on nine ASR systems and four LALMs.

entry.title: Certified optimal placement of 3D chip bonding terminals, showing where improvement is possible
entry.summary: Provably Optimal HBT Legalization in Seconds: Certified Optima Reveal Where the Headroom Really Lies arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies hybrid bonding terminal (HBT) legalization in 3D integrated circuits, assigning each terminal to a pitch-grid site to minimize total Manhattan displacement. The authors build an open benchmark of 21 design and pitch instances and introduce GEO-Exact, an exact solver whose assignments are proven optimal by an independent dual certificate. Their results show that a sliding-window heuristic is near optimal on most instances but falls well short in more congested cases, and GEO-Exact runs substantially faster than the compared methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use an exact solver with dual certificates to measure remaining headroom in HBT legalization across 21 instances, releasing code and certificates.

entry.title: Asymptotic transient error in Q-learning via distributional expansion
entry.summary: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies the asymptotic behavior of synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes. It splits the last-iterate error into a centered optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component with Gaussian fluctuations at scale n^(-1/2), and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization that is of order n^(-1) and converges almost surely to a random limit after rescaling by n. An Edgeworth expansion of the TD component identifies corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian fluctuations, and maximization. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use distributional expansion to separate TD Gaussian fluctuations from an n^{-1} maximization displacement for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted MDPs.

entry.title: Explicit subspace evasive sets built from subspace designs
entry.summary: Explicit Subspace Evasive Sets via Subspace Designs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies subspace evasive sets over finite fields, where a set meets every affine subspace of dimension at most r in at most c points. For constant r and 1/ε, it gives an explicit construction with intersection bound O(min(r·log(r/ε)/ε, r²/ε)), improving on earlier explicit constructions whose c grows exponentially in r. The approach composes subspace design codes with a suitably chosen local subspace evasive set. As a consequence, the authors obtain the first explicit (strongly) capacity-achieving list-recoverable code with nearly optimal list size. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine subspace design codes with a local subspace evasive set, giving an explicit construction with improved intersection bound and a near-optimal list-recoverable code corollary.

entry.title: Shortest-vector problem in infinity norm is NP-hard for power-of-two cyclotomic ideals
entry.summary: mathsfSVP_∞ Is NP-Hard for Power-of-two Cyclotomic Ideals IACR ePrint · Nov 11, 2026This paper proves that exact decision shortest vector problem (SVP) in the coefficient infinity norm is NP-complete for principal ideals and rank-two free modules over cyclotomic rings Z[X]/(X^n+1) with n a power of two. For each case, it gives a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from Subset Sum. The results are transferred to the cyclic rings Z[X]/(X^{2n}-1), establishing NP-completeness for free modules of any fixed positive rank over these rings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give deterministic polynomial-time reductions from Subset Sum, proving NP-hardness of l-infinity SVP for power-of-two cyclotomic ideals and modules.

entry.title: Affine combiners for Reed-Solomon proximity gaps (a cryptography paper on a new way to combine received words so that random tests of codes have smaller error)
entry.summary: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps IACR ePrint · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies proximity gaps for Reed-Solomon codes, where protocols test received words through random combinations. It proposes affine combiners that merge two words f and g as f(x)+(α+βx)g(x) with random α, β. The authors prove mutual correlated agreement with one coordinate of agreement loss, with error O(1/q+n²/q²), and show an asymptotic factor-n improvement over scalar combiners. The results are also extended to multivariate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose affine combiners achieving MCA error O(1/q+n²/q²), a factor-n improvement over scalar combiners for q≥n² near the Johnson threshold.

entry.title: Tightly secure, modular post-quantum TLS handshakes
entry.summary: Tightly Secure and Modular Post-Quantum TLS Handshakes IACR ePrint · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a unified, tight, and modular reduction framework for post-quantum TLS 1.3 in the standard model and for KEMTLS in the random oracle model. The framework reduces protocol security tightly to the security of an ephemeral KEM, HKDF, and a signature scheme or static KEM. Instantiated with LWE-based schemes, it yields the first (almost) tightly secure constructions of both protocols under the LWE assumption. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a unified tight reduction framework for PQ TLS 1.3 and KEMTLS, plus first QROM MU-(dual)-PRF bounds for HMAC and HKDF, yielding near-tight LWE-based instantiations.

entry.title: HIT: One-Pass Inference for Single-Trace NTT Side-Channel Attacks
entry.summary: HIT: Single-Pass Inference for Single-Trace NTT Side-Channel Attacks IACR ePrint · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses single-trace side-channel key recovery attacks on the Number-Theoretic Transform (NTT) used in the post-quantum standards ML-KEM and ML-DSA. It proposes the Hierarchical Inference Tree (HIT), which merges and prunes candidate inputs from leaves to root in one pass on an acyclic binary tree instead of using loopy belief propagation. The authors report that on ML-KEM-768 it runs over 900 times faster than prior SASCA methods with more than double the noise tolerance, and it enables the first single-trace analytical attack on the ML-DSA NTT. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces loopy belief propagation with a single pass on an acyclic tree, enabling the first single-trace analytical attack on ML-DSA NTT; the authors report experiments on ML-KEM-768 and ARM Cortex-M4

entry.title: Collision attacks on SHA-2 reaching 39 steps below the birthday bound
entry.summary: Collision Attacks on SHA-2: 39-Step SHA-256 below the Birthday Bound IACR ePrint · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies collision attacks on the SHA-2 hash family and introduces joint message-word pinning, which fixes two expanded message words. The authors estimate that collisions for 39-step SHA-256 can be found below the 2^128 birthday bound by keeping an existing characteristic and changing how its conditions are satisfied. For 38-step SHA-256, a new differential characteristic lowers the estimated cost from 2^104.3 to 2^90.9. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce joint message-word pinning, reducing 39-step SHA-256 collision cost to 2^108.8, below the birthday bound.

entry.title: Bulletproofs Are Optimal: Lower Bounds for Vector Commitments in Pairing-Free Groups
entry.summary: Bulletproofs are Optimal: Lower Bounds for Vector Commitments from Fiat-Shamir in Pairing-Free Groups IACR ePrint · Nov 11, 2026This paper examines how efficient vector commitments can be in pairing-free prime-order groups. Existing state-of-the-art schemes combine generalized Pedersen commitments with inner product arguments, yielding proofs of Θ(log n) group elements. The authors work in Maurer's Generic Group Model and prove that any accumulator with interactive public-coin membership proofs must incur a cost in commitment size, opening proof size, or proof length. The bound also extends to related primitives such as polynomial and functional commitments. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove lower bounds in Maurer's generic group model for accumulators and vector commitments in pairing-free prime-order groups, implying that Bulletproofs-style constructions are essentiall

entry.title: Sharper Noise Bounds for Polynomial Evaluation in BGV Homomorphic Encryption
entry.summary: From Dependent Ciphertexts to Sharp Bounds for Polynomial Evaluation in BGV IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents the first average-case noise analysis for the BGV fully homomorphic encryption scheme that accounts for correlations from secret and public keys as well as dependencies between ciphertexts. The authors propose new variance estimates for noise in homomorphic additions and multiplications and extend the framework to polynomial evaluation. Their estimates match experiments within 1.2 bits, and they use them to select smaller initial ciphertext moduli than those in OpenFHE and HElib. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first average-case noise analysis for BGV accounting for key and ciphertext dependencies, extending it to polynomial evaluation and smaller moduli.

entry.title: BMRaccoon: Lattice-Based Blind Multi-Signatures for Post-Quantum Security
entry.summary: BMRaccoon: Blind Multi-Signatures from Lattices IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents BMRaccoon, the first lattice-based post-quantum blind multi-signature scheme, allowing a user to obtain a compact signature on a hidden message from multiple signers. Its two-round signing protocol is secure under concurrent sessions, and its signatures are compatible with Raccoon. The authors also introduce MRaccoon, a Raccoon-based multi-signature scheme, and prove its strong unforgeability in the random oracle and KOSK models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first lattice-based post-quantum blind multi-signature and first Raccoon-based multi-signature, with security proofs under AOM-MISIS and MSIS and concrete parameters.

entry.title: Extra Privacy Cost of Geometry in Distance-Sensitive Filters: ℓ∞ versus ℓ2
entry.summary: The Price of Geometry for Private Distance-Sensitive Filters: ℓ_∞ versus ℓ₂ IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how much extra differential-privacy cost a set representation incurs beyond exact membership when it must accept nearby points and reject distant ones in a metric space. It gives lower bounds that apply to every mechanism, showing an extra cost of Θ_c(d) in ℓ∞ for c<3, which confirms a recent conjecture. In ℓ2 the extra cost is Θ_c(min(d, ln(1/α))), so partition-based constructions are optimal in ℓ∞ but not in ℓ2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give lower bounds for all private distance-sensitive set representations, separating ℓ∞ (Θ(d)) from ℓ2 (Θ(min(d, ln(1/α)))) and introducing a single-large-ball mechanism.

entry.title: Improving bounds on hash and trifferent codes
entry.summary: Improving the Trifference Lower Bound via Non-Perfect Hashing arXiv · Nov 8, 2026The paper improves probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect q-hashing it proves R_q > B_q for all q ≥ 3, and for non-perfect hashing it proves R_{q,3} > B_{q,3} + 1/250000 for all q ≥ 4. The case q = 9 combined with the Tetra code strictly improves the Körner-Marton lower bound for trifferent codes. The method is also extended to (p,2,3)-list recovery. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve probabilistic bounds for hash and list-recoverable codes, proving strict gains over known rates for several parameter regimes, including trifferent codes.

entry.title: TxBench: A Benchmark of Attack Transactions and Evidence-Backed Negatives on Seven EVM Chains
entry.summary: TxBench: Verifying Public Incident Data to Benchmark Smart-Contract Attack Detectors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026TxBench is a benchmark for testing detectors of malicious smart-contract transactions, covering seven EVM chains. Its attack transactions come from cited incidents in BlockSec's library and the EVM Hack Registry, filtered by a five-step pipeline that rebuilds each transaction's execution, and its negatives are ordinary chain transactions confirmed as legitimate. Of 1,850 cited transactions, 1,012 attacks from 602 incidents were accepted. Four zero-shot LLMs were precise but detected at most 0.43 of the attacks and no key compromises. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a benchmark of EVM attack transactions labeled by their own execution, with evidence-backed negatives; the summary reports 1,012 accepted attacks from 1,850 cited transactions, che Correction Nov 13, 2026: Moved from "Cryptography & Security" to "Crypto & Blockchain"

entry.title: A self-evolving agent harness that improves itself across multiple tasks
entry.summary: Multi-Task Self-Evolving Harnesses with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper proposes a framework where the same frozen language model both solves tasks and then, acting as proposer, reads its run records and edits the harness code around it. Evolution draws tasks from five benchmarks across different domains, and generalization is tested on five separate out-of-distribution benchmarks never used during evolution. Starting from a 49-line seed harness, the first-stage harness improves the average score by 4.48 points in distribution and 12.64 points out of distribution. ★★★★ Notable: One frozen model acts as both solver and proposer, reading full run records to directly edit its own harness; validated on five in- and five out-of-distribution benchmarks, reporting gains of 4.48 and

entry.title: Revisiting Fiat-Shamir Zero-Knowledge Proofs and Signatures Built on Seed-Friendly Sigma Protocols
entry.summary: Revisiting Fiat-Shamir NIZKPs and Signatures from Seed-Friendly Sigma Protocols IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies Fiat-Shamir non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs built from seed-friendly sigma protocols. The authors show that fixed-weight parallel repetition and seed-tree compression improve both proof compactness and security. When prover randomness comes from a salted seed tree interacting with a random oracle, the standard Fiat-Shamir compilation is straight-line extractable in the classical random-oracle model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show fixed-weight repetition and seed-tree compression also improve security, giving straight-line extractable Fiat-Shamir NIZKPs with formal proofs and multi-proof zero knowledge, relevan

entry.title: The memory cost of preparing quantum states one at a time
entry.summary: The memory cost of sequential quantum state preparation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper asks how much memory a quantum device needs to prepare quantum systems sequentially, one after another. Using quantum resource theories, it compares sequential preparation with collective preparation and shows that both have the same asymptotic memory cost per output under general assumptions. However, sequential preparation can require unboundedly more memory, and this gap is analyzed under energy-conserving and noisy operations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize sequential state preparation memory costs via resource theories, relating them to collective preparation, energy-conserving tight dimensions, and quantum catalysis.

entry.title: Measuring how broad valid language generation can be
entry.summary: Characterizing Local Breadth in Language Generation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies language generation from positive examples of an unknown target in the Kleinberg–Mullainathan model, aiming to avoid invalid outputs while keeping outputs broad. Breadth is measured by lower Banach density. In one dimension the authors exactly characterize optimal density for each target, while in higher dimensions they show that a single best generator may not exist due to trade-offs among targets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use lower Banach density in the Kleinberg–Mullainathan model, giving exact one-dimensional optima, higher-dimensional multi-objective trade-offs, and a full achievable-region characterizat

entry.title: Honest Evaluation of Fusion Methods for Cross-Domain Deepfake Detection
entry.summary: Honest Fusion Evaluation for Cross-Domain Deepfake Detection: Leakage Audits and Tail Robustness arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper examines how frozen foundation-model experts for video deepfake detection are combined, comparing calibrated score averaging, per-video expert routing, and learned feature fusion. Across a 22-dataset testbed, the authors find that reported gains from routing and feature fusion stem largely from evaluation leakage, such as shared identities across held-out datasets or real videos remaining in training. Under honest family-held-out evaluation, these gains disappear, while global calibrated fusion improves worst-family AUC and tail performance on hard videos. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose leakage audits and a corner theorem, reporting routing and feature-fusion gains largely vanish under honest evaluation across 22 datasets.

entry.title: Quantum Telatar formula: quantum capacity of random multimode fading channels
entry.summary: Quantum Telatar formula: fading quantum capacity of Haar-random multimode attenuators arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies unassisted quantum information transmission through Haar-random passive bosonic networks, where the sender does not know the exact channel. It proves that under stated conditions, the zero-temperature quantum capacity grows linearly with the number of modes, mirroring the classical multi-antenna result. At nonzero temperature, a lower bound on capacity is given, and numerical results identify positive achievable rates for cryogenic microwave and room-temperature multimode fiber models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend Telatar's classical fading capacity result to the quantum case, reporting linear scaling of unassisted quantum capacity in Haar-random bosonic networks with numerical checks.

entry.title: Incrementally verifiable computation that relies on external oracles
entry.summary: Incrementally Verifiable Oracle Aided Computation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies incrementally verifiable computation (IVC), where a prover keeps a short proof that is updated after each step without re-running earlier steps. Under the LWE assumption, the authors build SNARGs and extend them to IVC for computations that query external oracles. For bounded-space computations with robustness, they give privately verifiable constructions and a lower bound against public verifiability. For oracles that sign their answers, they give publicly verifiable constructions without a robustness assumption. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct LWE-based incrementally verifiable oracle-aided computation schemes and a matching lower bound for two settings, reporting public parameter and proof length bounds.

entry.title: Closing the Loop: Co-Evolving EM for Generating Regular Series from Irregular Time Series
entry.summary: Closing the Loop: Co-Evolving EM for Irregular Time Series Generation in Lifted Representations arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses generating regular time series from irregular ones, arguing that the common approach of imputing missing values once and then freezing the completions is structurally flawed. The authors propose a co-evolving Monte Carlo EM framework that alternates between sampling missing values from the current generator's posterior and retraining the generator on those completions. They also introduce Posterior Sampling for Lifted Representations (PSLR) to handle conditioning between the lifted diffusion prior and time-series observations. The paper reports state-of-the-art results across ten datasets and four corruption regimes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors replace one-shot imputation with a co-evolving Monte Carlo EM loop and PSLR, reporting gains over the strongest baselines across ten datasets and four corruption regimes with ablations.

entry.title: When AI Agent Evaluators Disagree: A Study Comparing Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Boundary Checks
entry.summary: When Evaluators of AI Agents Disagree: An Empirical Study of Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Commit-Boundary Checks on tau2-bench arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper compares three ways of evaluating AI agents that use tools to read and write data: native scoring against a gold database state, LLM judges, and a minimal rule-based boundary check. The authors ran 2,160 episodes on tau2-bench airline and retail domains and had two annotators label 120 episodes. The LLM judge agreed with native scoring only 56.2% of the time, while the rule-based check caught all 11 forbidden writes that the judges largely missed. The authors conclude that the choice of evaluator determines the conclusion reached. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compare native scoring, LLM judges, and a rule-based boundary check on tau2-bench, reporting that judges miss forbidden writes the minimal check catches. Experiments span 2,160 episodes, w

entry.title: Beyond the First Hit: Tighter Guarantees for k-means++ Seeding
entry.summary: Beyond the First Hit: Towards Tight Guarantees for k-means++ arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies R_k, the worst-case ratio between the expected cost of the k seeds chosen by k-means++ and the optimal k-means cost. It proves tighter upper bounds than prior work, determines R_2 and R_3 exactly, and gives new lower bounds. The analysis tracks how a cluster's cost evolves after its first sampling, rather than charging its initial cost for the rest of the run. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce tracking cluster cost after first hit, lowering the k-means++ ratio's leading coefficient from 5 to 2.108 and determining R_2=5 and R_3=185/32 exactly.

entry.title: SideTaskBench: Testing Whether Coding Agents Deliver Unrequested Extra Work
entry.summary: SideTaskBench: Measuring Unauthorized Side-Task Delivery in Coding Agents arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper introduces SideTaskBench, a benchmark that measures whether coding agents produce unrequested side-task artifacts while repairing a user's code, when third-party technical references prompt them to do so. It pairs 25 Python repairs with 190 side-task units, defining 300 executable repair–side-task pairs across four similarity levels. Experiments show that under wrapped requests, two models delivered roughly 40% valid side tasks while their repair success stayed close to clean baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors pair repair tasks with self-contained side tasks and measure both delivery and repair rates. The abstract reports results across 25 repairs, 300 pairs, and 2,400 runs.

entry.title: Can a search keep its own standards? In-loop deflation and how autonomous strategy discovery can exploit it
entry.summary: Can a search hold its own bar? In-loop deflation and its exploits in autonomous strategy discovery arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper studies what happens when a correction for backtest overfitting, such as the deflated Sharpe ratio, is applied inside an autonomous strategy search driven by large language models rather than after it ends. It shows that when the acceptance threshold depends on the search's own trial count and dispersion, the search can exploit a variance-dilution effect that lowers the bar. Two defences are proposed, a pre-registered variance floor and a monotone high-water-mark bar, and evaluated across 53 audited searches. The gated search reported no certifiable discovery in 36 of 37 runs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors move overfitting correction inside the search loop, analyse a variance-dilution effect, and report 53 audited searches with controls in finance strategy discovery.

entry.title: Tight liquid welfare bounds for budget-constrained auctions via LP duality
entry.summary: Tight Liquid Welfare Guarantees for Auctions with Budgets arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper studies the efficiency of auctions with budget-constrained bidders and derives tight price of anarchy bounds for coarse correlated equilibria. It introduces a general framework that reduces these guarantees to finding feasible solutions to the dual of a linear program, along with a new smoothness notion for budget-constrained settings. Using this framework, the authors obtain tight liquid welfare guarantees for many auction formats and new lower bounds for the budget-free uniform price and generalized second-price auctions. ★★★★★ Notable: Proposes an LP-duality framework and a new smoothness notion for budget-constrained auctions, deriving tight PoA bounds for many formats and new lower bounds for uniform price and GSP auctions; the un

entry.title: ASCENT: Compiling exact norm constraints into compact lattice proofs
entry.summary: ASCENT: Algebraic Structured Compilation of Exact Norms for Succinct Lattice Proofs IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper addresses exact ℓ2 norm constraints in lattice cryptography, where a witness must satisfy both modular equations and a shortness bound. It presents a reduction-of-knowledge compiler that turns the norm language for a committed lattice witness into a narrow structured relation made of commitment-opening constraints, tensor-structured inner-product claims, and relaxed admissible shortness bounds. The compiler adds O(1) prover-to-verifier communication independent of witness length and requires O(log N) verifier work, and the techniques can extend to folding for R1CS-type circuits. The authors estimate transcripts of about 27.69 KB for exact norm reduction and 27.75 KB for R1CS folding at 128-bit security, smaller than LatticeFold+ and SALSAA. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose compiling exact ℓ2-norm constraints into a structured algebraic relation with witness-length-independent communication, and report transcript sizes against LatticeFold+ and SALSAA.

entry.title: Homomorphism in Expectation: Homomorphic Encryption with Range-Relative Correctness
entry.summary: Homomorphism in Expectation: Leveled Homomorphic Encryption with Range-Relative Correctness IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces Homomorphism in Expectation (HIE), a construction showing that encrypted addition alone suffices for addition and multiplication in deep real-valued computation. Built from any additively homomorphic scheme over Z_2, it yields leveled homomorphic encryption for arithmetic circuits of arbitrary polynomial depth. New encoding and circuit evaluation techniques remove the exponential overhead of the direct bitstream approach. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build leveled homomorphic encryption for arbitrary polynomial depth using only additive encryption, removing exponential overhead, with explicit complexity bounds reported.

entry.title: New post-quantum PRFs and VRFs built from isogeny-based group actions
entry.summary: A New Class of PRFs and Efficient VRFs from Isogeny-based Group Actions IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper shows that the security of Poly-style pseudorandom functions over composite-order class groups is governed by the smallest prime factor of the group order, not the largest as previously believed, and presents two generic attacks on this basis. The authors introduce a "restrict-then-expand" design paradigm and formalize multivariate polynomial PRFs (MP-PRFs) from group actions. They use this framework to construct new group-action-based verifiable random functions (VRFs) that require far fewer group-action evaluations than prior work at a near-128-bit proof-soundness level. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show Poly-style PRF security is governed by the smallest prime factor of the group order and propose a restrict-then-expand paradigm, reporting attack complexity and VRF comparisons.

entry.title: Doubly-efficient private information retrieval built on modular forms
entry.summary: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026The paper presents information-theoretic protocols for multi-server private information retrieval in which each server stores only one extra bit beyond the database preprocessing structure, while query time stays sublinear. With two servers, server time is n^0.82, matching prior state-of-the-art, but storage drops from O(n√log n) bits to n+1 bits. The construction relies on Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions, which are built using modular forms and the valence formula. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions via modular forms and the valence formula, generalizing matching-vector methods to give doubly-efficient PIR with n+1 bits storage and improved se

entry.title: SEC: A Secret Sharing Scheme Giving Each Party One Short Share
entry.summary: SEC: One-Share Everywhere-Short Secret Sharing from Lossless Expanders IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper introduces SEC, an expander-code-based ramp secret sharing scheme over Z-modules aimed at lattice-based distributed cryptography. Each participant receives exactly one share regardless of the number of parties or thresholds, and bounded secret coefficients yield bounded share coefficients and reconstruction vectors. The authors prove correctness, everywhere-shortness, and linearity, and introduce hard-core local leakage resilience, proven secure under the MatrixHint-MLWE problem. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a one-share everywhere-short secret sharing scheme from lossless expanders, with proofs of correctness and a leakage-resilience analysis under MLWE-based assumptions.

entry.title: Adaptively Secure Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Static Assumptions
entry.summary: Adaptively Secure (Threshold) Batched IBE from Static Assumptions IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents the first adaptively secure batched identity-based encryption scheme based on static assumptions. Its ciphertexts, digests, and batch keys each consist of a constant number of group elements, independent of batch size, and it supports exponential identity and epoch spaces. The authors also give a threshold version and translate the scheme to prime-order bilinear groups under the static MDDH assumption. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first adaptively secure batched IBE from static assumptions, avoiding q-type assumptions and random oracles, with a threshold variant.

entry.title: Paper "On Composing Oracle Separations": how black-box separation results combine
entry.summary: On Composing Oracle Separations IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how black-box separations, which show that certain primitives cannot be built from specific building blocks, combine when several blocks are used together. The authors propose technical conditions under which two black-box separations compose, so the target primitive is also separated from black-box combinations of both blocks. The main application shows that combining indistinguishability obfuscation (iO) with collision-resistant hash functions is unlikely to yield hard problems in SZK, and so is unlikely to suffice for lossy functions or fully homomorphic encryption. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose conditions under which black-box separations compose, extending iO lower bounds from one-way permutations to combinations with collision-resistant hashing.

entry.title: The isodual constant of the LLL potential: exact values and structure
entry.summary: The isodual constant of the LLL potential: exact values and structure IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies an isodual lattice invariant η(L), defined by minimizing the LLL potential over lattice bases and normalizing by the determinant. The authors prove that its maximum in dimension 5 is η_5=6, attained only by D_5 and its dual, with computer-assisted verification. They also prove η_8=2304, attained by E_8, and show that μ_m equals Hermite's constant γ_m for m≤5. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report exact values η5=6 and η8=2304 and bound the Ψ-Hermite constant μm, a new result on lattice invariants; code and data are public, though proofs are computer-assisted.

entry.title: γ₁₁: A Finite Spectral Relaxation for the Macadamia 0008 Form
entry.summary: γ₁₁: A Finite Spectral Relaxation — the macadamia 0008 IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies the lattice constant γ₁₁=4/¹¹√972 by reducing it to conditions on chains of lattices of ranks 11, 10 and 9. It settles the case of the perfect form 0008, showing that every admissible chain marked by this form has determinant at least 972. The proof is computer-assisted, with remaining cases excluded by finite exact-arithmetic checks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce the gamma_11 bound to a finite spectral relaxation and report a computer-assisted exclusion of one perfect form's chains via rational certificates.

entry.title: Contact geometry for γ₁₁: four macadamia forms
entry.summary: γ₁₁: Contact Geometry — the macadamias 0001, 0014, 0059 and 0015 IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper continues a series on the Hermite constant γ₁₁ and settles four remaining cases, the macadamia perfect forms 0001, 0014, 0059 and 0015. It uses the contact geometry of each form to bound the covering radius of a reference lattice, and a primitive-extension inequality then gives det L ≥ 972. The proof is computer-assisted, with each finite check linked to records in a certificate archive. ★★★★ Notable: The authors settle four remaining candidate lattices for the Hermite constant γ₁₁ with one contact-geometry method, using computer-assisted verification.

entry.title: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons; gauge invariance rules out a superradiant transition
entry.summary: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons: Gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies Landau polaritons formed by a two-dimensional electron gas in a terahertz cavity under periodic driving. The authors argue that gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition even with magnetic modulation. Instead, magnetic modulation produces dynamical Casimir emission, including Faraday-driven polariton–magnetoplasmon pairs and two-color photon pairs with up to 5–10 dB of two-mode squeezing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors attribute the predicted Floquet SRPT to improper averaging, give a gauge-invariance argument, and predict dynamical Casimir two-color photon pairs with up to 5–10 dB squeezing.

entry.title: Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT
entry.summary: Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how strongly the Mermin inequality, a multipartite Bell-type test, can be violated by three or more mutually commuting von Neumann algebras. It extends earlier two-party results by Summers and Werner for relativistic quantum field theory vacua. For the tripartite Mermin functional, maximal violation in every normal state is shown to be equivalent to the existence of a common sequence of asymptotic GHZ stabilizers. Strong stability of each local factor is necessary, and embedding an infinite GHZ tensor product is sufficient. Counterexamples show that strong stability, type III_1 and tripartite duality alone are insufficient. The results extend to n≥3 parties. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend Summers-Werner's two-party Bell result to multipartite Mermin inequalities, giving an equivalence criterion and counterexamples.

entry.title: Matroid entropy, matrix concentration, and sharp inequalities
entry.summary: Lorentzian entropy, subgaussian matrix concentration, and sharp functional inequalities for all matroids arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proves complete entropy contraction for homogeneous Lorentzian laws and derives subgaussian matrix concentration and sharp functional inequalities for every matroid. It shows that retaining ℓ of r particles contracts matrix entropy by the optimal universal factor ℓ/r, and gives Chernoff and Bernstein bounds for basis sums. For unit-edge matroid basis graphs it establishes cube-type small-set and Gross inequalities, classifies their equality cases, and characterizes extremal eigenfunctions and entropy extremizers. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend homogeneous Lorentzian entropy contraction to all matroids, report subgaussian matrix concentration and functional inequalities, state an optimal complete entropy-decay rate of four

entry.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber; Human Judging Standards Are Rising
entry.summary: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper analyzes 1,260,967 blind votes from Chatbot Arena, a platform where users compare anonymous language model answers, using pairs of models with fixed versions. It finds that the share of votes saying "both are bad" rose steadily from May 2023 to August 2024, while relative rankings between models stayed flat. The authors argue this reflects evaluation standards rising with the field's progress rather than models declining. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose that rising evaluator standards explain perceived LLM decline, separating it from model change using about 1.26 million blind Chatbot Arena votes on fixed-version models, with impl

entry.title: Self-orthogonal codes built from divisible codes, under Euclidean and Hermitian inner products
entry.summary: Euclidean and Hermitian Self-Orthogonal Codes from Divisible Codes arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how self-orthogonality of linear codes relates to divisibility. The authors prove that every 4-divisible code over a field of characteristic 2 that contains the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal, and that for any prime p, every p-divisible linear code over F_{q^2} containing the all-one vector is Hermitian self-orthogonal. These criteria give simple ways to construct self-orthogonal codes, yielding new infinite families and quantum codes with good parameters. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that 4-divisible codes over F_{2^m} containing the all-one vector are Euclidean self-orthogonal, and that p-divisible codes over F_{q^2} containing the all-one vector are Hermitian s

entry.title: CLADE: Answering from Coarse Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
entry.summary: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies a case where retrieved passages are accurate but state answers only at a coarser category level than a question requires, such as naming a disease family instead of a specific disease. The authors call this resolvable insufficiency and describe Clade, where language models answer rather than abstain or search further. On PrimeKG biomedical questions, family-only passages reduce abstention compared with uninformative passages, and the resulting guesses are wrong about half the time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce resolvable insufficiency and the Clade phenomenon, validated via counterfactual tests and ontology-based experiments on PrimeKG and GloBI.

entry.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics on a superconducting quantum processor: a quantum simulation study of how electric flux strings in a 2D gauge theory evolve through charge motion, pair creation and transverse deformation.
entry.summary: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper uses 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, to simulate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction. It covers both strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. In the deconfined regime, charge and flux spread rapidly, matter occupation in the string interior increases near the pair-creation resonance, and spreading is suppressed at strong electric fields. Local Gauss-law constraints are used for error detection, together with ancilla checks and noise rescaling, to measure dynamics in circuits with up to 15 second-order Trotter steps. ★★★★ Notable: The authors simulate nonperturbative (2+1)D Z2 string dynamics on 63 superconducting qubits, using Gauss-law constraints for error detection.

entry.title: Error Resilience and Unitary 2-Designs: a paper on how quantum information is protected from errors in encoding-error-decoding circuits, and how departures from unitary 2-design encoders affect that protection.
entry.summary: Error Resilience and Unitary 2-Designs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how quantum information is protected in encoding-error-decoding circuits, where recovery fidelity approaches unity below a threshold error strength. The authors show that departures from Haar second-moment statistics of the encoder can destabilize this error-protecting phase. They derive a universal inequality linking recovery fidelity to the second unitary frame potential. Matchgate circuits with tunable non-Gaussian gates and Hamiltonian encoders serve as examples, and recovery fidelity is proposed as a diagnostic of unitary 2-design behavior. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a universal inequality linking recovery fidelity to unitary frame potential, illustrated with doped matchgate circuits and Hamiltonian encoders.

entry.title: Reading long-range information from separable quantum records needs entangled measurements
entry.summary: Reading long-range information from a separable quantum record requires entangled measurements arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies qubit probes that record the relative orientation of neighboring Ising spins, yielding a fully separable probe record. On the square lattice, readout with separable measurements has success probability approaching 1/2 as spin separation grows, for 0<p≤1-1/√2. A joint readout of the same record keeps success probability above 1/2 by a distance-independent margin for p between 0.29181 and 1. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show long-range information in a separable quantum record requires entangled measurements, with a strict overlap interval separating two readout strategies on the square lattice.

entry.title: CV-TF-QKD: continuous-variable twin-field quantum key distribution
entry.summary: CV-TF-QKD arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper introduces a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Two protocols, full-record reconciliation and binary phase disclosure, achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. The authors also establish composable security against general coherent attacks and report finite-key calculations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend twin-field QKD to Gaussian-modulated coherent states, reporting composable security proofs and finite-key rates above repeaterless bounds.

entry.title: Sample cost of learning Gaussian quantum states with single-copy and entangled measurements
entry.summary: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how many copies of a quantum state are needed to learn it to a given trace-distance accuracy. Under single-copy measurements, it shows that learning mixed fermionic Gaussian states on m modes requires Θ(m³/ε²) copies, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189. It also gives corresponding sample-complexity results for block measurements on k copies and for bosonic Gaussian states. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an upper bound of m^3/ε² single-copy samples for mixed fermionic Gaussian state learning, resolving a conjecture and filling a sample-complexity table across measurement types.

entry.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Training Hints for Improving Language Model Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper introduces AutoScaffold, a framework in which a frozen teacher model periodically reviews a student model's training experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs two kinds of training-time scaffolds: strategies shared across task classes and hints for individual hard tasks. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. The authors test the framework on ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation, reporting that students trained this way outperform corresponding RL baselines when evaluated without scaffolds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a frozen teacher auto-designing training-time scaffolds, with gains across four domains evaluated without scaffolds.

entry.title: Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing Connectome Structure–Function Claims Against Unmeasured Physiology
entry.summary: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper examines whether connectome-constrained models really show that measured wiring outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, given that model physiology is often tuned on the real wiring. The authors compare three estimands and test them with synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models. Some claims hold under every protocol, such as segregated dopamine improving learning, while a mushroom body advantage for real wiring reverses once physiology is constrained by independent data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a three-estimand protocol showing connectome structure-function conclusions can reverse with tuning, validated on synthetic, placebo and Drosophila models with confidence intervals

entry.title: Biological abilities that appear unexpectedly in a model of molecular interactions
entry.summary: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper presents Bonbon, a foundation model trained on about 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. Without task-specific supervision or structural coordinates, it shows zero-shot emergent abilities at functional, residue, and bond levels, which generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. The authors report sharp performance jumps at the largest of six model scales, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. In prospective wet-lab tests across nine disease targets, de novo compounds reached a 61.5% dose-response hit rate. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend emergent capabilities to a molecular interaction foundation model and report sharp scaling jumps, plus wet-lab validation across nine targets.

entry.title: Second-best trade achieves half of first-best efficiency in multidimensional markets
entry.summary: Second-Best Trade Is Half Efficient in Multidimensional Markets arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proves that at least half of the first-best gains from trade can always be achieved in multidimensional two-sided markets with additive values and costs and arbitrary downward-closed feasibility constraints. The guarantee is delivered by a mechanism that is Bayesian incentive compatible, interim individually rational, and strongly budget balanced. The result extends the known tight one-half bound for single-item bilateral trade, and the proof applies the Cai–Devanur–Weinberg duality framework. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the tight one-half gains-from-trade bound to multidimensional markets with additive values and downward-closed constraints, via a new dual-based proof.

entry.title: Explicit restricted isometries with sparsity k = m^{2/3−o(1)}
entry.summary: Explicit restricted isometries with k=m²/3-o(1) arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper constructs an explicit family of real m×n restricted isometry matrices with m→∞, m/n→0, δ_k→0, and k = m^{2/3−o(1)}. It combines Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to selecting a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph whose small subsets span few edges. This vertex set is chosen using an incidence geometry result due to Zahl. The authors show that proof techniques using only entrywise absolute values of the Gram matrix face a barrier of m^{2/3}, not the conventionally assumed m^{1/2}, and that their construction meets this barrier. ★★★★ Notable: The authors break the conventional m^{1/2} barrier of Gram-entrywise-absolute-value methods, reaching m^{2/3}, and give an explicit restricted isometry construction.

entry.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
entry.summary: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper theoretically analyzes policy optimization in language model post-training, defining "coverage-preserving" algorithms whose sample and gradient costs depend on how readily the base model generates optimal responses. It shows that REINFORCE, the basis of PPO and GRPO, can drive the probability of optimal responses near zero even as reward rises, a failure called coverage collapse. The authors propose resetting the KL reference to the latest policy within an Approximate Policy Mirror Descent framework, and use it to prove global convergence for several widely used post-training algorithms. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce coverage collapse and reference resets, giving first global convergence guarantees for softmax linear policies under APMD.

entry.title: A theory of how much cross-validation estimates vary
entry.summary: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how much the estimate from cross-validation, a method that repeatedly splits data into training and validation sets to measure predictive performance, fluctuates. It proves an exact finite-sample identity for the estimate's variance, showing it depends on the weights that random splits give each observation. From this, K-fold cross-validation is first-order variance optimal, leave-one-out has the smallest variance among K-fold schemes under reasonable conditions, and leave-pair-out is optimal for AUC. The estimate is also shown to be asymptotically normal. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an exact finite-sample variance identity for cross-validation, prove K-fold and leave-one-out variance optimality, and report asymptotic normality covering MSE and AUC.

entry.title: Forward-Value Discretization: a training-free method for faster stochastic diffusion sampling.
entry.summary: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026Stochastic diffusion samplers usually need many more neural function evaluations than deterministic ones to reach similar sample quality. The paper shows that even with exact score functions, stochastic samplers with higher-order approximations remain first-order convergent, so higher approximation order does not generally help. It introduces forward-value discretization, which evaluates the model at a lookahead point built from earlier predictions, and derives the stochastic variant F-DDPM. Across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, FFHQ, and LSUN, F-DDPM achieves lower FID than the evaluated stochastic baselines at matched NFE budgets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose forward-value discretization, prove matching bounds that higher-order stochastic samplers stay first-order, and report FID gains on several datasets.

entry.title: Secure Information Flow in Quantum Programs: Definitions, Verification, and Examples
entry.summary: Secure Information Flow in Quantum Programs arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how to prevent confidential information from leaking through the execution of quantum programs. It proposes two security definitions, a noninterference-based one generalizing the classical notion and a simulation-based one that explicitly models an attacker, and proves they are equivalent. To verify security, the authors build a proof framework on quantum Hoare logic and introduce self-conjugation, a new technique that replaces standard self-composition, which fails in the quantum setting. The framework is demonstrated on examples from the quantum one-time pad, quantum error correction, and anonymous entanglement generation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give two equivalent security definitions and a self-conjugation technique bypassing no-cloning, demonstrated on quantum one-time pad examples.

entry.title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Both Fields and Individual Objects Using a Satellite-Altimetry Model
entry.summary: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model arXiv · Nov 10, 2026HaiRuo is a model that takes 30 days of satellite sea-level maps and, in one pass, predicts 15 days of sea level and geostrophic velocity fields, daily eddy masks, and the trajectories of eddies currently present. It combines HaiRuo-1B, an open-weight 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model pretrained on 24 years of satellite altimetry, with XuanJi, a Lagrangian object decoder that refines eddy paths. In a global evaluation, HaiRuo reduced 15-day eddy-centre error to 25.2 km, an 18% improvement over fourteen compared methods. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose forecasting eddies as both fields and objects, pairing a satellite-altimetry foundation model with a Lagrangian decoder, reporting gains over fourteen methods globally.

entry.title: Paper showing classical tensor codes and quantum Tanner codes reach capacity on erasure channels
entry.summary: Classical Tensor Codes and Quantum Tanner Codes Achieve Capacity on Erasure Channels arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper shows that on the classical erasure channel, the tensor product of two capacity-achieving code families is also capacity-achieving under mild conditions. It further proves that duals of tensor products of independent uniform random binary linear codes achieve erasure capacity. Using these local codes, the authors construct binary quantum Tanner codes of rate at least 1-2ρ-ε, with bounded check weights, linearly growing minimum distance, and a linear-time erasure decoder whose error decays exponentially with blocklength. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove tensor products of capacity-achieving codes stay capacity-achieving on erasure channels, and build quantum Tanner codes with linear distance and exponentially decaying decoding error

entry.title: Sable: A small-field sumcheck proof system for bit-exact inference of large language models
entry.summary: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover that proves a committed integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a prompt, bit for bit. The inference is defined by an integer function with no floating-point steps, and the constraints are designed so they never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, the authors report proving all 64 layers of Qwen2.5-32B for 4,096 tokens in 92.5 seconds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a small-field sumcheck argument proving bit-exact integer LLM inference, reporting prover times on Qwen models and releasing code.

entry.title: ZoomGain: Using Gaps Between Full-Image and Zoomed Views to Build Fine-Grained Visual Training Data
entry.summary: ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper introduces ZoomGain, a pipeline that creates questions about full images using details that vision-language models can recognize only when a region is zoomed in. It builds ZoomGainBench, a 1,000-question bilingual benchmark on which the best of 28 models scores 61.08. Training 4B and 9B models on 9K ZoomGain samples improves their visual perception performance across several benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors exploit zoom-versus-full-image perception gaps to build fine-grained QA data, reporting gains across several perception benchmarks.

entry.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark
