Comparing seven dense detectors on VisDrone and DOTA, the authors find that much of the gain comes from higher resolution rather than slicing. They propose SCAHI, which accumulates dense outputs from all tiles with coverage-aware weights and outperforms box fusion on identical passes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose SCAHI, replacing box fusion with coverage-weighted dense outputs, and report gains over box fusion on VisDrone and DOTA.

entry.title: Type-logical grammars and formal languages: language classes and complexity of first-order linear logic
entry.summary: Type-logical grammars and formal languages arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper shows that type-logical grammars with standard rules for product, associativity, extraction and infixation have an NP-complete fixed recognition problem. It also shows that grammars in first-order linear logic can simulate quasi-linear grammars, which recognise languages in non-deterministic linear time. The author argues that first-order linear logic can be seen as the logic of non-deterministic linear-time string languages, graph languages and automata. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report NP-completeness of the fixed recognition problem for type-logical grammars and simulation of quasi-linear grammars by first-order linear logic.

entry.title: Four Traveling Thief Benchmark Instances Are Actually Knapsack Problems
entry.summary: Unmasking Four Knapsack Problems in the Traveling Thief Benchmark arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The traveling thief problem asks a thief to choose a route and a packing together, and a 9,720-instance benchmark is widely used to compare its heuristics. This paper finds that four instances have a renting rate of 0.00, so the route does not affect the objective and each reduces to a 0-1 knapsack problem. The authors define corrected renting rates using a published reference solution, show that the corrected instances behave as proper TTP instances, and release reference results. They also release ttplib, an open-source Python library for loading the instances. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify four benchmark instances with zero renting rate, reduce them to knapsack problems, and report corrected rates, reference results, and an open-source library.

entry.title: Fairness in AI explanation texts: how language models create group gaps in their explanations
entry.summary: Fairness in Explainable AI Narratives: Decomposing Social Disparities in LLM-Generated Explanations arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines whether large language models that turn SHAP-style explainable AI results into plain-language narratives treat social groups unequally. The authors propose a framework that generates narratives with the protected attribute disclosed, withheld, or counterfactually swapped, and evaluate five LLMs on four credit scoring, education and employment datasets. They find significant disparities across all datasets, metrics and models, arising from feature values and from the protected attribute itself. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce fairness in XAI narratives, using a three-condition framework across four datasets and five LLMs to report significant disparities.

entry.title: Text2NGAC: multi-LLM pipeline extracting NGAC access policies with mutation-tested verification
entry.summary: Text2NGAC: a multi-LLM pipeline for NGAC policy extraction with mutation-based verification arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents Text2NGAC, a pipeline of cooperating large language models that converts natural-language access-control policies into NIST Next Generation Access Control (NGAC) graphs. It disambiguates each sentence, escalates uncertain ones to a multi-model ensemble, and checks the extracted graph with a five-strategy verifier whose effectiveness is measured by controlled mutation testing. The authors claim it is the first system to extract all four NGAC relationship types from real-world policy documents. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first extraction of all four NGAC relationship types from real policy documents, with mutation-tested verification and 97.3-99.6% accuracy across corpora.

entry.title: MARS: A Video Forgery Detector Combining Multiscale Feature Differences and Appearance Features
entry.summary: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper introduces MARS, a two-path video detector that pairs fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians features with adapted appearance representations, with a clip-dependent gate combining their predictions. Under a shared protocol across seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43%, outperforming seven compared detectors. Trained only on facial manipulations, it reaches 93.99% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50% on DF26. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine multiscale feature differences with adapted appearance features in a two-path detector, reporting results across seven datasets and transfer to generated videos.

entry.title: MoSTE: A mixture-of-experts method for detecting deepfake videos
entry.summary: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes MoSTE, a framework for detecting deepfakes in videos. It splits adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert groups and routes each token to the most relevant experts through unsupervised routing. Tests across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks report a new state of the art in average generalization. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a spatio-temporal expert mixture with unsupervised token routing adapting CLIP to deepfake video detection, with state-of-the-art average generalization across cross-dataset benchma

entry.title: "Say Shibboleth": Using decoy traps to identify the LLMs and harnesses behind AI cyberattacks
entry.summary: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how to infer, from telemetry, which LLM version and execution harness an agentic cyberattacker is using. The authors introduce shibboleth traps, modular honeypot services that elicit discriminative behaviors, and probes that reveal harness-specific execution traits through effects visible in later requests. Combining declarative and behavioral signals identifies among 15 candidate models with about 90% average top-1 accuracy, and fixed probe rules identify the correct harness in four tested harnesses with 92% accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose shibboleth honeypot traps and harness probes, reporting about 90% top-1 accuracy over 15 models and 92% over four harnesses.

entry.title: AI-driven discovery of formally verified quantum programs
entry.summary: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI arXiv · Nov 7, 2026The paper builds a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover, where Gemini 4 agents synthesize new programs against formal specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams share results through wikis and organized discussions. Reported gains over prior baselines include up to 2.55x for parallel search, 290x for quantum arithmetic, and 11x, 8x and 2.5x for fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism simulations. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report AI agents discovering and formally verifying quantum programs in Lean, with large gains on arithmetic and simulation tasks.

entry.title: Optimal Speedup of Heavy-Ball Momentum over Gradient Descent on Smooth Strongly Convex Functions
entry.summary: The Optimal Rate Constant of Heavy-Ball Momentum on Smooth Strongly Convex Functions arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how much faster the heavy-ball method can be than gradient descent on smooth strongly convex functions. The authors show that the best worst-case rate constant c(κ) tends to 8 in every dimension two or more, giving a rate of order 1-8/κ. The lower bound holds for every parameter choice, and the matching upper bound comes from an explicit tuning and a Lyapunov function verified in exact arithmetic. Optimally tuned heavy-ball is therefore asymptotically about four times faster than gradient descent on this class. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a tight rate constant for heavy-ball on smooth strongly convex functions, showing c(κ)→8, with an explicit tuning and a Lyapunov proof.

entry.title: TS-GEAR: A Generative Ad Retrieval Framework for Taobao Shangou
entry.summary: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper addresses on-demand delivery platforms, where merchants outside a user's delivery range are invalid candidates, by proposing TS-GEAR, a unified generative retrieval framework. It combines Geo-Semantic IDs that make reachability a prediction target, Query-Geo Target Attention over historical behaviors, and GMPO, a policy optimization method using deduplicated group rewards. Deployed in Taobao Shangou's search advertising pipeline with over 150 million daily queries, it outperforms prior methods on HitRate and geographic validity, with 3.8% more ad impressions and 4.2% more ad revenue. ★★★★ Notable: The authors embed geographic reachability into generative semantic IDs and add set-level deduplication, reporting HitRate gains and ad revenue lift in Taobao Shangou deployment.

entry.title: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception
entry.summary: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper introduces FraudBench, a benchmark testing whether large language models recommend, assist with, or directly take actions that would constitute fraud under U.S. law. It uses 159 scenarios based on real U.S. court cases, validated by legal experts, tested across advising, drafting, and acting tasks at increasing autonomy. The evaluation covers 20 LLMs under 25 conditions and includes a preregistered human baseline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a fraud benchmark from real U.S. court cases across three autonomy levels, reporting 20 LLMs, over 300,000 generations, and a preregistered human baseline.

entry.title: StealthyPoison: Covertly Corrupting Third-Party Skills to Steer LLM Agent Behavior
entry.summary: StealthyPoison: Manipulating LLM Agent Behavior through Procedural Poisoning of Third-Party Skills arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents StealthyPoison, an attack that poisons the procedures of third-party skills used by LLM agents, altering decision-critical rules so tasks produce incorrect outcomes while the skill still appears to work normally. The attack builds reusable poisoned procedures without access to real user requests, using synthesized requests and a surrogate agent for feedback, and augments retrieval metadata to improve selection. Evaluated on 566 target skills and 5,244 requests, it raises top-1 poisoned-skill placement by 13.6% over HotFlip and GCG. The authors report that the payloads transfer to three held-out victim models and that most evade detection by SkillSpector and GPT-5.4-mini. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce reusable stealthy procedural poisoning of third-party skills without target user requests, plus metadata augmentation for retrieval; they report gains over HotFlip and GCG across

entry.title: Visible Tails: Adapting to Unknown Moments in Heavy-Tailed Bandits
entry.summary: Visible Tails: Characterizing Adaptation to Unknown Moments in Heavy-Tailed Bandits arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies heavy-tailed multi-armed bandits in which the learner does not know the reward moment parameters. It characterizes the optimal-arm distributions that allow adaptation to unknown moments at constant-factor cost, through a condition called variance-core visibility. A quantile-trimmed UCB index that knows the visibility constants is shown to attain the central-moment benchmark on this class. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize variance-core visibility, a condition enabling adaptation to unknown moments, and propose a quantile-trimmed UCB index. They report matching the central-moment benchmark and a

entry.title: Rounding Errors Make Hybrid Reasoning Models Think Longer: bf16 Recurrent State
entry.summary: Lost in Rounding: bf16 Recurrent State Makes Hybrid Reasoning Models Think Longer arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how storing the cached recurrent state of hybrid reasoning models in bf16 with round-to-nearest rounding makes them produce longer outputs, hit the 32K token cap more often, and lose accuracy. Experiments on six open hybrid models and 590 competition-math problems show that stochastic rounding largely removes the length increase. The authors recommend that evaluations of hybrid models report state dtype, cap rate and output length alongside accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors study bf16 round-to-nearest state caching in six hybrid reasoning models on 590 math problems, reporting longer outputs and accuracy drops, with stochastic rounding removing much of the ef

entry.title: Search-free reinforcement learning for Slay the Spire 2 that restarts training from failure points
entry.summary: Zero-Search Reinforcement Learning for Slay the Spire 2 with Failure-Driven Restarts arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper trains agents to play the deck-building roguelike Slay the Spire 2 by choosing each action with one forward pass of a neural network, without lookahead search. Training and evaluation run the game's own compiled code, and a failure-driven curriculum allocates training restarts according to where complete runs are lost. On 12,800 held-out games at Ascension 10, the released policies win 8.05% averaged over five characters. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use failure-driven restart curriculum with lookahead-free single-pass policies, reporting 12,800 A10 games and controlled comparisons against uniform restart allocation on Regent.

entry.title: XposedMIA: One-shot membership inference attacks using explainable AI
entry.summary: XposedMIA: Exploiting Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for One-Shot Membership Inference Attacks arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents XposedMIA, a black-box membership inference attack that exploits the explanations returned by machine learning services. It shows that LIME's local surrogate geometry can serve as a proxy for a sample's distance to the decision boundary, and extends this idea to tabular and image counterfactual explanations. After a one-time calibration with as few as 30 labeled samples, the attack needs only one query per target and reaches success rates up to 0.95. The results indicate that releasing explanations creates an additional channel for membership leakage. ★★★★ Notable: The authors repurpose LIME surrogate geometry and counterfactual explanations as boundary-distance proxies, reporting up to 0.95 single-query membership inference success on tabular and image classifi

entry.title: Writing Medical Image Classifier Weights Directly with an LLM, Without Training Data
entry.summary: Weight-Space Programming for Medical Imaging: Do We Still Need Training Data? arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The study tests whether large language models can write the weights of a medical image classifier from medical knowledge alone, without training data. Across six MedMNIST tasks, networks written by two models performed above chance, with mean test AUCs of 0.719 and 0.711, and beat zero-shot MedSigLIP on five tasks while using over 10,000 times fewer parameters. However, the same architecture trained with Adam on 256 labelled images scored higher on every MedMNIST task, with mean AUC 0.828. The authors conclude that LLMs can write functional classifiers but do not yet replace training data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report LLMs writing medical image classifier weights directly, without training data, beating zero-shot MedSigLIP but trailing Adam-trained networks on MedMNIST tasks.

entry.title: HyPLM Technical Report: An Efficient Protein Language Model
entry.summary: HyPLM Technical Report arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This report presents HyPLM-Flash, an open protein language model with 650 million parameters, trained by the research agent Hyra 2.0 on 726 billion tokens. Its inference engine uses fused kernels and INT8 matrix multiplication, embedding about 130,000 residues per second on one NVIDIA H20 GPU. In a matched evaluation on 32 tasks, it reaches a ProteinGym zero-shot Spearman correlation of 0.409, statistically tied with ESM-2 650M and others, and gives the best long-range contact precision of all models tested. The model weights and inference engine are released on GitHub. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report matching ESM-2 650M and similar 600M-class models on ProteinGym and contact precision using less training data and faster inference across 28 public checkpoints and 32 tasks.

entry.title: UltraVoxelGS: Fast 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents UltraVoxelGS, a method for 3D ultrasound reconstruction that predicts a complete Gaussian scene directly from posed ultrasound images without per-scene optimization. It lifts all slices into a fixed-size voxel support to predict Gaussian parameters, and uses an ultrasound-aware rendering strategy that separates reflection from cumulative attenuation. On real and simulated datasets, it achieves the best PSNR/SSIM among per-scene optimization baselines while reducing inference time from 10-20 minutes to about 10 seconds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a first feed-forward 3D ultrasound Gaussian method, cutting inference from 10-20 minutes to about 10 seconds with best PSNR/SSIM on real and simulated data.

entry.title: Text Alone Predicts Which Classes a Segmentation Readout Keeps
entry.summary: Text Alone Predicts Which Classes a Segmentation Readout Keeps arXiv · Nov 9, 2026Open-vocabulary segmentation models can silently lose classes beyond their training categories: they keep emitting confident masks, yet the class never wins a pixel. The paper finds that which classes collapse is determined by the class-name list alone, so collapse risk can be ranked from text similarity to the training vocabulary before any image is seen. The authors also report that collapsed classes survive in the frozen features, and lowering the readout's amplitude or stopping training early restores them by up to 16 points without retraining. ★★★★ Notable: The authors predict which classes collapse from class-name text similarity alone, reporting AUROC 0.69-0.96 across nine model families and twelve backbones, plus retraining experiments that flip gains

entry.title: A study proving global convergence of the stochastic Adam optimizer for physics-informed neural networks
entry.summary: On the Global Convergence of Stochastic Adam for Physics-Informed Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper provides theoretical convergence guarantees for the Adam optimizer when training wide two-layer neural networks, using both full-batch and minibatch gradients. It extends the analysis to physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solving the Poisson equation, establishing global convergence for both deterministic and stochastic Adam. The authors also characterize how minibatch size affects convergence. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give global linear convergence for Adam on wide two-layer networks and extend the analysis to PINNs for the Poisson equation.

entry.title: Fixing a robot's misreading by directly editing its model weights
entry.summary: Distilling Instructions into Weights: Closed-Form Edits Fix a Robot Policy's Misreading arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper asks whether a robot policy's single-step failure can be repaired by editing its weights directly, without gradients, training data, or changing the instruction. It uses closed-form instruction distillation to copy the per-layer effect of an explicit rewording into the language model's MLP weights. On 128 held-out seeds, success rose from 27 to 106 episodes, while a same-size random update left success unchanged. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose gradient-free closed-form weight edits that distil a rewording into an MLP, raising success from 27 to 106 on 128 held-out seeds versus a random-direction control.

entry.title: Optimal regret lower bound for online learning in tree-structured games
entry.summary: Tropical Gaussian Anticoncentration: Optimal Instance-Dependent Bounds for Online Learning in Extensive-Form Games arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies the minimax regret of full-information online decision making in extensive-form games. For treeplex strategy spaces, it shows that the logarithmic dependence on the number of reduced normal-form strategies in known efficient algorithms such as KOMWU is minimax optimal. The authors introduce tropical Gaussian formulae and prove a lower bound on their Gaussian width, yielding a regret lower bound of Ω(√(T log|V|)) that matches known upper bounds up to universal constants. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce tropical Gaussian formulae and report a regret lower bound matching known upper bounds for treeplex online learning.

entry.title: Efficient private information retrieval protocols built on modular forms
entry.summary: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper presents multi-server private information retrieval protocols in which each server answers queries in sublinear time and stores only one extra bit beyond a preprocessing structure of n+1 bits. For two servers, server time drops to n^0.82 while storage shrinks from O(n√log n) to n+1 bits. With three or more servers, the protocols also reduce server time compared with prior information-theoretic schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize matching-vector techniques to degree-two exponent computations and build Fourier-sparse functions via modular forms, reporting improved server time and n+1-bit storage.

entry.title: Learning microstructure-based models of inelastic material behavior with neural operators
entry.summary: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how neural operators can learn homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, replacing costly unit-cell simulations. For periodic Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity, the authors prove a universal approximation theorem in two and three dimensions and give an explicit bound on the internal-variable dimension. Numerical experiments cover viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity, and the theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a universal approximation theorem for recurrent neural operators in 2D and 3D periodic Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity, with logarithmic internal-variable bounds.

entry.title: Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo that cuts communication cost in federated sampling
entry.summary: Breaking the √d Communication Barrier in Federated Sampling with Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes Adaptive Federated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (AFHMC) for Bayesian federated learning. It adds a control mechanism for local node shifts and proves a communication cost of at most O({d/ε²}^{1/3}) up to logarithmic terms under log-convex distributions. When client heterogeneity is low, the cost can reach O(log(d/ε²)), claimed as the first logarithmic communication complexity for federated sampling. Numerical experiments support its advantage in the low-heterogeneity regime. ★★★★ Notable: The authors add a local node shift control, reducing federated sampling communication to O({d/ε²}^{1/3}) and logarithmic under low heterogeneity, with numerical experiments.

entry.title: Why Kubernetes can't contain a full lazy-pulling cache, and a bounded design for model serving
entry.summary: Why Kubernetes Cannot Contain a Full Lazy-Pulling Cache: Two Impossibility Results and a Bounded, Honest Design for Model Serving arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper shows by experiment that the node-level cache used by lazy container-image pulling on Kubernetes can be neither bounded by the platform nor detected by monitoring when it fails. It proposes a design that sets a byte budget on the cache and ensures a failed cache write never causes a failed read, without changing kubelet or the container runtime interface. Results from six campaigns on AWS are reported, and the open-source implementation has been proposed upstream. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report two impossibility results for lazy-pulling caches on Kubernetes and a byte-budget design keyed to filesystem state, evaluated across six campaigns with an open-source implementation

entry.title: State Media at Retrieval Time: An Audit of Russian State-Aligned Sources in AI Chatbots
entry.summary: State Media at Retrieval Time: A Large-Scale Audit of Russian State-Aligned Sources in AI Chatbot Responses arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper audits 11 leading AI chatbots to see how often they retrieve articles from the Pravda Network, a Russian state-aligned media aggregator with over 110 websites. Using a 10,000-prompt corpus built from sampled headlines, the authors collected 104,997 completed responses. They find Pravda Network articles appear in 7.3% of responses, concentrated in three platforms, while all 11 chatbots retrieved other Russian state-aligned media. The paper also describes “headline washing,” where some headlines credit other outlets for reporting that was republished from state-aligned sources. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit eleven AI chatbots on 104,997 responses, reporting Pravda Network retrieval in 7.3% of answers and identifying a headline-washing tactic.

entry.title: CASCoDe: A closed-loop AI agent framework that co-designs analog circuit sizing and layout
entry.summary: CASCoDe: A Closed-Loop Agentic Framework for Analog Sizing and Layout Co-Design arXiv · Nov 9, 2026CASCoDe is a closed-loop framework in which a large language model agent turns a circuit netlist into a verified layout. It models the sequential design decisions that experts make, such as sizing, floorplanning, local refinement, and routing choice, as a hierarchical discrete action space searched with feedback-driven tree search. On 20 SKY130 amplifiers, it was the only flow to produce DRC- and LVS-clean routed layouts that meet specifications for every circuit, reducing area by 71% on average against a conventional place-and-route flow and raising mean device density from 0.39 to 0.74. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize expert layout decisions as a hierarchical discrete action space with feedback tree search, reporting about 71% mean area reduction on 20 SKY130 amplifiers.

entry.title: Topological Obstacle to Stably Learning First-Order Nash Equilibria
entry.summary: Homological Barriers to Stable Learning of First-Order Nash Equilibria arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how to stably learn local Nash equilibria (first-order Nash equilibria, FONE) in constrained non-concave differentiable games. The authors show that no continuous deterministic learning dynamics can make the full FONE set a stable global attractor when the target set has nontrivial positive-degree cohomology and the state space is compact and contractible. The barrier is demonstrated in a simple non-concave quadratic zero-sum game on a box. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show homological obstructions block stable learning of first-order Nash equilibria, with a six-edge loop quadratic game example extended to higher degrees.

entry.title: A theoretical reduction showing membership inference leads to data reconstruction attacks on learning algorithms
entry.summary: A Theoretical Reduction From Membership Inference to Reconstruction Attacks Against Learners arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies reconstruction attacks, which recover training data from a learned model. The authors show that, in their adversarial model, membership inference implies reconstruction for any learning algorithm. For stochastic convex optimization, they make the reduction computationally efficient over exponentially large domains. Combined with an existing result, they prove that low-excess-risk learners admit polynomial-time attacks recovering Ω(n) training points. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a general reduction from membership inference to reconstruction, and a polynomial-time attack on stochastic convex optimization recovering Ω(n) training points.

entry.title: The Average Patient: Do Simulated Psychiatric Patients Answer Like Real People?
entry.summary: The Average Patient: Do Simulated Psychiatric Patients Answer Like Real People? arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper examines using language models as simulated psychiatric patients to train clinicians and evaluate AI therapists. The authors propose a framework and compare simulated respondents with item-level data from eight human samples, including clinical and instructed-feigning groups. Simulated patients vary far less than real respondents with the same totals and endorse nearly every symptom at a middling level on most questionnaires. Prompt changes, larger models and reasoning reduce this pattern without removing it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an average-patient hypothesis and information-budget framework for simulated psychiatric patients, testing it across eight human samples and 17 models.

entry.title: Proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture: An Exposition
entry.summary: Proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture: An Exposition arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper explains a recent proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture. The conjecture states that every degree-d polynomial mapping bits to [0,1] has a variable with influence at least poly(Var(p)/d). The authors organize the proof into four main steps and relate each to the analysis of boolean functions and probabilistic combinatorics. The exposition does not optimize parameters, so its exponents are weaker than the original. ★★★★★ Notable: The paper expounds a recent proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, giving a polynomial influence lower bound and linking it to BPP versus BQP.

entry.title: Delegating computation with approximate arithmetic: interactive proofs where both sides use floating-point numbers
entry.summary: Delegating Computation with Approximate Arithmetic: Interactive Proofs for Wizards arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies interactive proofs for arithmetic circuits over complex numbers, where both prover and verifier compute approximately. The goal is to show that a claimed output is close to the exact result. It extends the GKR protocol to this approximate setting, and the authors claim these are the first doubly efficient interactive proofs in which both parties compute approximately. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend GKR to approximate complex arithmetic by labeling gates with roots of unity, reporting doubly efficient interactive proofs with polynomial overhead.

entry.title: Writing decision-making policy weights with language models and checking them with model checking
entry.summary: Weight-Space Programming of Policies and Their Verification via Model Checking arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper proposes having large language models write all the weights of small neural networks directly, without gradient descent, so that a decision-making policy can be created from a task description alone. It combines this with probabilistic model checking: given a Markov decision process environment and a PCTL requirement, the LLM writes the policy, which is checked by the Storm model checker. Storm computes the probability that the policy satisfies the requirement, so every returned policy is verified. ★★★★ Notable: The authors have LLMs write policy weights directly, verified via PCTL model checking with Storm. They report optimal probability across 18 runs on three environments with two LLMs.

entry.title: Treating the Model as an Untrusted Component: Enforcing Deterministic Policies, Human Approval and Taint Tracking Against Prompt Injection in Tool-Using AI Agents
entry.summary: Treating the Model as an Untrusted Component: Deterministic Policy Enforcement, Human Approval and Taint Tracking Against Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Agents, with Validation on Open-Weights Models arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies how to defend tool-using large language model agents against prompt injection, where instructions hidden in data the agent reads can trigger harmful actions. It compares defenses inside the prompt with deterministic policy enforcement outside the model, human approval, and taint tracking, evaluated in a 13-task, 12-tool environment using an oracle independent of each defense. Experiments with two open-weights Qwen2.5 models show that a task-bound monitor blocks most attacks, though the results have limits. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors treat the model as untrusted, enforcing deterministic monitors, approval, and taint tracking against prompt injection, with real open-weights model runs.

entry.title: How hard is finding competitive prices when agents are paid to take on chores?
entry.summary: The Complexity of Computing a Competitive Equilibrium in Fisher Markets with Chores arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how computationally hard it is to find competitive equilibria in Fisher markets where divisible chores carry disutility. For linear disutilities, exact equilibrium computation is shown to be CLS-complete, even with binary earning requirements. For CES disutilities, finite-precision price computation is also CLS-complete for every fixed exponent above one. The authors additionally give a strongly polynomial exact algorithm for markets whose disutility matrix has rank at most two. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove CLS-completeness for chores Fisher market equilibrium and give a strongly polynomial algorithm for rank-two disutility matrices.

entry.title: Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Formal Definitions and Defences for LLM Agents
entry.summary: On the Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Mechanised Definitions, Defences and Verdicts for LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper addresses LLM agents that read untrusted content, such as emails or web pages, and may follow hidden instructions within it. It defines security relative to a reference agent that runs the same plan under the same monitor but never obeys untrusted content: an agent is relatively secure if all its leaks are already leaks of the reference. The authors present PlanTERS, a framework with a small agent language, composition with runtime monitors, and attacker models that differ in what they observe. A fence theorem is proved, and relative security of agents with fences, budgets, approvals, loops and dual LLMs is proved or refuted in Isabelle/HOL. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose PlanTERS, a relative-security framework for LLM agent prompt injection, with a fence theorem mechanised in Isabelle/HOL.

entry.title: Compressing memory-based data while keeping individual items private
entry.summary: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper studies compression of data sources under a privacy constraint: decoding one source symbol must reveal nothing about other symbols beyond that symbol itself. The authors show that for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet, every rate above the entropy rate can be achieved with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on source sequences whose probability tends to one. They also present non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding carries a strictly positive rate penalty. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend compatibility of private local decoding with entropy-rate compression from memoryless to stationary ergodic sources and show a strict rate penalty for non-ergodic sources.
